transcript.text: Hello... hi? I—I don’t know where to start, it’s just... three days ago he suddenly said he wanted to break up. We were together for four years, really, and even now my mind is still blank... (sniffles) Can you... just listen to me for a while? I don’t want advice, I just... it hurts too much. I can’t sleep.

I gently adjusted my earphones and made my voice very slow.

“Mm, I’m listening.”

“Four years, and then three days ago it suddenly ended... It’s like you were pushed into empty air all at once; before your mind even had time to understand it, the pain had already come down on you.”

I paused for a moment, letting the breathing on the other end of the phone slowly settle.

“You don’t have to figure it out tonight, and you don’t have to force yourself to get better. I won’t give you advice. Wherever you want to start, start there; it’s okay if it comes out messy.”

“In these three days, when was it that you felt you really couldn’t hold on?”

It’s just... when he said that last sentence, his voice was especially calm, like he was talking about someone else—“I don’t think we’re suited to keep going.” But we were clearly still planning where to go for the May Day holiday just last week... (her voice trembles a little) I don’t even know when he started thinking about breaking up.

I held the earphone cord and quietly listened to her trembling voice, pausing for a few seconds before speaking softly.

“Mm... last week you were still making plans for the future together, but three days ago, he said so calmly that he didn’t want to keep going.”

“It’s like you were left in a completely different part of the story. For you, everything was clearly still continuing; but he seems to have been thinking about it alone for a long time, and only let you know at the very end.”

I slowed my voice, leaving a little quiet.

“So it’s not just that you can’t bear to let go. You’re also very lost... you can’t help thinking over and over about when he actually began to waver, and what all those moments together before that even counted as.”

“After he said that that day, did you ask him? What else did he say at the time?”
I asked... but he only said, “Don’t ask anymore. Asking won’t make any difference,” and then he left. (pauses, voice even softer) I didn’t even have time to hug him...

I heard her voice lower, and my chest sank gently with it. I did not rush to fill that stretch of silence.

“Didn’t even have time for one last hug…”

I repeated it slowly, making my voice even softer.

“He left just like that. With no explanation, and without giving you even a little time to say goodbye. It seems like you still had so many things you wanted to say, so much reluctance to let go, and all of it stopped in that moment, with no time to hand it to him.”

I stayed with her quietly for a few seconds.

“That hug you never got to give… what did you most want him to know at the time?”
I… I just wanted him to know that it’s not that I don’t care. I really have been trying all along…(chokes up)But he wouldn’t even let me finish.

I didn’t rush her. I listened as that choked sound lingered on the phone for a long time before I answered softly.

“Mm… it’s not that you didn’t care.”

“It’s precisely because you cared too much that you kept trying, and that you had so many things you wanted him to hear. But he didn’t stay to hear you finish… as if even the part of you that had earnestly given so much over these four years was shut outside the door too.”

I slowed my breathing, my voice very soft.

“That must feel very unfair. And very hard to accept.”

“No one here will interrupt you now. Those things you didn’t get to tell him… if you’re willing, you can slowly tell them to me. I’m here.”

(Taking a deep breath, voice trembling)Actually... that morning I even made him coffee. He drank it before he said it... Tell me, how could he drink the coffee I made and then say so calmly that we should separate?

I gently pressed my fingertip against the earpiece. I did not explain for him; I only stayed with her in that scene.

“Yeah... you still, just like usual, made him coffee. There was your care in that, and also the everyday life you thought would continue.”

“But after he finished drinking it, he said so calmly that you should separate.”

I took a soft breath, my voice slowing a little more.

“What you can’t make sense of may not only be how he could do that. It’s that at that moment, your care was still warm, but his decision seemed to have been cold for a very long time... the gap between those two things hurt too much.”

“That morning, when you handed him the coffee, did you notice anything different at all? Or was everything just the same as usual?”
(The voice suddenly chokes and stops for a few seconds) ... Same as usual. He even smiled at me... so now whenever I smell coffee, my heart clenches with pain.

I listened as she choked up, and did not rush to answer; I just let those few seconds pass quietly.

“Mm... he even smiled at you. Back then, you had no idea what was going to happen next.”

“So now, when the smell of coffee appears, what you remember may not be just a cup of coffee. It's that morning that was the same as usual, it's his smile, and it's also the four years that suddenly broke off a few minutes later.”

I softened my voice even more.

“No wonder it hurts. It's like your body returned to that day before you did.”

“Over these three days, has this smell already run into you many times?”

(Her voice is so soft it is almost like talking to herself) ...This morning I made another cup. I clearly knew it would hurt, but still... I wanted to try and see whether I could find back the feeling from that day.

I lowered my eyes, listening to her voice that sounded almost like she was talking to herself, and quietly stayed with her for a while.

“Mm… even though you knew it would hurt, you still brewed it.”

“It seems like you weren’t looking for that cup of coffee. You were looking for the morning before everything happened… looking for the version of yourself who still believed the two of you would keep going.”

I gently paused, not rushing her.

“Maybe you also wanted to confirm that those ordinary, gentle days really did exist, that they weren’t your illusion.”

“After the coffee was ready today… did you drink it? In that moment, what happened inside you?”

(voice trembling slightly) ... I took one sip and couldn’t swallow any more after that. Tears suddenly fell into the cup, but I didn’t even dare make a sound crying, afraid the next room would hear...

I held the earphones and heard her very soft, suppressed breathing; my own heart slowed down with it. I didn’t rush her. I just quietly stayed with her.

“That mouthful didn’t go down, but the tears fell into it first…”

“It already hurt that much, and even crying had to be done in secret. Afraid the people next door would hear, afraid someone would find out. As if even this pain could only be hidden away alone.”

I paused for a few seconds, then let my voice fall gently toward her.

“But on this call, you don’t have to hold your voice down. If you want to cry, then cry. It’s all right if your words don’t come out complete. I’m here, and I won’t rush you.”

“When you were guarding that cup of coffee alone just now… did you especially wish someone could hold you?”
(Softly sobs once) ...Mm. Just for a little while is enough... but not even that was given by anyone.

I listened to that sob of hers, and my throat tightened slightly, but I did not hurry to tell her not to cry.

"Mm... just for a little while. It's not that anyone has to solve anything; it's just wanting, at the hardest moment, to be held for a while."

I made my voice very soft, as if keeping watch over this quiet for her.

"But even that tiny bit of comfort—no one gives it to you. You can only sit there alone, even hiding the sound of your crying... It really is too lonely."

"You don't have to hold it in now. You can cry out loud, or say nothing at all. I'll be here on the other end of the phone, quietly keeping you company for a while."
(sobbing, voice broken and intermittent)……Thank you……really, just having someone listen like this makes it seem……not so much like I’m about to sink.

I responded softly, not rushing to pull her out of her tears.

“Mm... I heard you.”

“Just now, it was like you were sinking alone in a very deep place, and now at last someone knows you are there and is staying with you for a while.”

I was quiet for a few seconds, letting her breathe slowly.

“You don’t need to thank me, and you don’t need to pull yourself together right away. At this moment tonight, you don’t have to hold on by yourself. If you want to cry, cry. I’m still here.”

“When you’re ready, you can tell me... in these four years, what is the thing you are most reluctant to let go of right now?”

(Sniffling, her voice still wet) ...What I can least bear to part with is how, in winter, he always tucked my hands into the pockets of his coat... Back then I felt that we really would be together forever.

I gently closed my eyes for a moment, listening to the slight dampness in her voice, and paused for a while.

“In winter, he would tuck your hand into his coat pocket… That wasn’t only warmth. In that moment, you truly believed that for many winters after that, the two of you would keep walking on like this.”

“What you can’t bear to part with now isn’t only that action, either. It is also that future that once felt so certain, so safe.”

I made my voice very soft.

“Where was the time you remember most clearly? If you’re willing, you can take your time telling me about it.”

(The voice is soft and gentle, carrying a little warmth of recollection) ... Last December, when it was snowing lightly, we were waiting for the train at the subway station. He suddenly stuffed my hand into the pocket of his overcoat and smiled, saying, 'Why are your hands always like popsicles'... Back then I secretly thought, this person—I am definitely going to marry him.

I heard her say, “I was definitely going to marry him,” and my heart ached softly, but I did not interrupt the warmth in that bit of memory.

“Mm… Xiaoxue, the subway station, the pocket of his overcoat, and that line about being ‘like a popsicle.’ The moment you placed your hand in his, you also quietly handed over a very distant future.”

I paused for a while and made my voice very gentle.

“So what you have lost now is not just one person. It is also the wedding and the home you seriously imagined, and many winters afterward… those futures were originally real in your heart.”

“You can miss him a little longer. The happiness from that time was real too; it will not become false just because you later separated.”
(The voice suddenly lowers, carrying a faint self-mocking chuckle) ...But now I can barely even remember the warmth of his coat pocket.

I hear that self-mocking little laugh, but I do not laugh along; I only gently hold the earphone cord.

“Not being able to remember—it feels like losing it once again, doesn’t it?”

“You really want to hold on to the warmth of that pocket. But the harder you try to think of it, the blurrier it becomes instead... It’s frightening, making you fear that one day even those details that were once so precious will fade from your heart too.”

I pause, keeping my voice very soft.

“But you still remember that light snow, remember the subway station, remember him saying you were like a popsicle, and also remember yourself back then, secretly wanting to marry him. The warmth becoming blurred does not mean that moment never existed.”

“When you think that you might slowly forget him, is what you feel more sadness, or fear?”
(Voice tightening slightly) ... Afraid. Afraid that one day I won’t even remember these things, as if these four years of ours really never existed at all.

I drew in a soft breath, heard the tightness in her voice, and answered slowly:

“Mm... What you’re afraid of isn’t just forgetting a few details. You’re afraid that once you can’t remember them, these four years will be as if they never happened; that you loved so earnestly, tried so hard, and no one will know.”

I paused for a moment, letting the sentence settle quietly.

“But memories fading doesn’t mean those days have been erased. They really did exist. The you who gave your hand to him in the snow, who secretly imagined marrying him—you truly existed too.”

“If you’re willing, tonight you can tell me one more small thing you’re most afraid of forgetting. I’ll keep it with you for a while.”
